args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api began failing health checks with an elevated error rate (~18%) across us-east, us-west, and eu-west. In response, all production regions were rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The rollback completed successfully and the service is verified healthy again on v2.3.0. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the cause of the health-check failures is identified.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

**Diagnosis**
- The latest production deploy of checkout-api, **v2.3.1**, was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%.
- The most recent release that was healthy in production was **v2.3.0** (the v2.3.1-rc was only a staging release and was never healthy anyway).

**Actions taken**
1. **Rolled back** checkout-api to **v2.3.0** in all production regions. Verified healthy again with an error rate of 0.2%.
2. **Opened a SEV2 incident** (INC-0001) for checkout-api documenting the health-check failures, the rollback to v2.3.0, and verification that the service is healthy post-rollback. The on-call engineer has been paged.

No change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production (the rollback policy only gates deploying versions never healthy in prod). Recommend the team investigate v2.3.1 before attempting another rollout.
